title: Randomized algorithms & hashing tricks
relevance: Medium — custom/`unordered_map` safety and pair-sum / set-hash tricks show up in OAs; random-sample & Zobrist are CF/AtCoder rating skills Striver never covers.
company_notes: Complementary power-of-two / target pair lookup → hash set in O(n), not O(n²) (1005C-style). Running D:K / reduced-fraction splits → hash pairs (a/g,b/g) (Diluc / Zero-Quantity family). Same multiset on two windows → sort+compare is the safe interview answer; Zobrist/sum-hash is the CF speed trick (ABC367F / Prefix Equality). Interactive with too few queries to scan → random sample then binary-search / walk from the best sample (LowerBound / AP / Subway Pursuit) — more CF-style company contests than classic phone screens.

phases.goal: Spot birthday collisions, random sample/pivot, and Zobrist/set-hash signals instead of a full deterministic scan.

must_hit.point: Signals: “≥ half / third of the range”, interactive query limits too small for full scans, “are these two sets/multisets equal?”, “is every frequency even / a multiple of 3?”, “find any collision among pairs”.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those wording cues and reaches for randomness or fingerprint hashing rather than a full scan.

must_hit.point: Birthday / pigeonhole: after ~√M samples into a space of size M you expect a collision — pair-sum equals, anti-hash sizing, “have I seen this fingerprint?”.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the √M-into-M collision intuition and ties it to pair-sum / fingerprint collision asks.

must_hit.point: “For each element, is there another that sums with it to a power of two / target?” → hash set with complementary lookup; interviewers expect O(n) with a set, not O(n²).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps complementary target/power-of-two lookup to an O(n) hash set, rejecting O(n²).

must_hit.point: Same-window multiset equality: sort+compare is the safe interview answer; Zobrist/sum-hash is the CF speed trick (ABC367F / Prefix Equality).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates interview-safe sort+compare from CF Zobrist/sum-hash for multiset equality.

probes: What wording makes you inject randomness or a set fingerprint instead of scanning everything?
Is this complementary pair lookup, reduced-ratio hashing, multiset equality, or an interactive sample/pivot?

hints.1: Listen for half/third density, too-few interactive queries, set/multiset equality, even/triple frequencies, or pair collisions.
hints.2: Map to birthday collision, random sample when a target is ≥1/k, Zobrist XOR/sum fingerprints, or complementary hash-set lookup.
hints.3: Say: signals are ≥ half/third, interactive caps, set/multiset equality, even/×3 frequencies, pair collisions; birthday ~√M into M; OA complement lookup is O(n) set not O(n²); multiset equality → sort+compare interview-safe, Zobrist/sum-hash for CF.

phases.goal: State birthday collision, random-sample/pivot verification, and Zobrist set vs multiset fingerprint plans.

must_hit.point: If a good object occupies ≥1/k of the space, pick O(k log(1/ε)) random candidates and verify (majority queries, interactive lower_bound, geometry).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the ≥1/k density → O(k log(1/ε)) sample-and-verify plan.

must_hit.point: Zobrist / XOR hashing: assign each value a random 64-bit id; XOR (or mod-P sum) fingerprints a set / parity-multiset — equal fingerprints ⇒ equal sets w.h.p.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes random 64-bit ids and XOR or mod-P sum as set/parity-multiset fingerprints with w.h.p. equality.

must_hit.point: Random pivot (Las Vegas): sample candidates, pick the best feasible pivot, finish with a short deterministic walk / recurse — Interactive LowerBound samples ~√n nodes then jumps from the best ≤x predecessor.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Outlines sample → best feasible pivot → short deterministic finish, citing the ~√n LowerBound shape.

must_hit.point: Sets use XOR of member ids (toggle add/remove with another XOR); multisets use + mod a big prime (or 128-bit) instead of XOR — Rearrange Query prefix sums, not XOR.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts XOR for sets with sum-mod for multisets and names the prefix-sum multiset template.

probes: How do you choose how many random candidates to try when a good object is ≥1/k of the space?
When is the fingerprint XOR versus a modular sum?

hints.1: Ask whether the target is dense enough to sample, or whether you need a set/multiset fingerprint.
hints.2: ≥1/k → O(k log(1/ε)) samples then verify; sets XOR; multisets +; pivots sample then walk from the best.
hints.3: Say: sample O(k log(1/ε)) when density ≥1/k and verify; Zobrist random 64-bit ids with XOR or mod-P sum; LowerBound-style pivot samples ~√n then walks from best ≤x; XOR toggles sets, + mod (or 128-bit) for multisets.

phases.goal: Code clock-seeded RNG, anti-hash maps, Zobrist fingerprints, and interactive flush hygiene.

must_hit.point: RNG: mt19937_64 rng(chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count()); + uniform_int_distribution; never fixed seeds on CF open-hacking; avoid raw rand() / RAND_MAX.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes clock-seeded mt19937_64 + uniform_int_distribution and rejects fixed seeds and raw rand().

must_hit.point: Anti-hash: custom hash for unordered_map / gp_hash_table (e.g. splitmix64 xor’d with a random salt); or just use map when TL allows.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names splitmix64+salt custom hash or falling back to map under TL.

must_hit.point: Zobrist template: h[v] = rng(); set hash = XOR of h[v] for members; toggle add/remove with another XOR; for multisets use + mod big prime (or 128-bit) instead of XOR.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes or narrates h[v]=rng(), XOR aggregate with toggle, and sum-mod for multisets.

must_hit.point: Interactive hygiene: flush (endl / cout.flush()), respect query caps, treat -1 as immediate exit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions flush, query caps, and exiting on -1.

probes: How do you seed the RNG and protect unordered_map on CF?
Walk through the Zobrist set-hash template and the multiset variant.

hints.1: Clock-seed the 64-bit engine; don’t leave unordered_map on its default hash.
hints.2: mt19937_64 from chrono; splitmix64+salt or map; h[v]=rng() then XOR or +; flush and handle -1.
hints.3: Say: mt19937_64 rng(chrono::steady_clock::now()...); uniform_int_distribution; never fixed seeds / raw rand(); splitmix64 xor salt or map; h[v]=rng(), XOR toggle for sets, + mod for multisets; endl/flush, exit on -1.

phases.goal: State birthday collision probability, sample-trial fail bounds, and expected pivot/query costs from the file.

must_hit.point: Birthday rule of thumb: collision among m hashes into modulus M has prob ~m²/M; for string/set fingerprints prefer 64-bit (2^61−1 or unsigned overflow) or two independent hashes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States ~m²/M and the 64-bit / double-hash safety preference.

must_hit.point: Random sample when a target occupies ≥1/k of positions: T ≈ k·ln(1/ε) trials ⇒ fail prob ≤ε; verify each candidate in O(log n) (position lists) or O(len).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives T ≈ k·ln(1/ε) with fail ≤ε and O(log n) or O(len) verify.

must_hit.point: Random pivot expected cost is O(√n) or O(n) depending on the problem (843B / Quickselect intuition); Tournament Countdown crowns a winner in expected O(n) queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites expected O(√n) or O(n) for pivots and expected O(n) for the tournament elimination.

probes: What collision probability do you budget for m fingerprints into modulus M?
How many trials do you need when a good object is ≥1/k of the space?

hints.1: Birthday is quadratic in the number of samples; density sampling is logarithmic in 1/ε.
hints.2: ~m²/M for collisions; T ≈ k·ln(1/ε) for ≥1/k hits; pivots expected O(√n) or O(n).
hints.3: Say: collision prob ~m²/M so prefer 64-bit (2^61−1 / unsigned) or two hashes; T ≈ k·ln(1/ε) ⇒ fail ≤ε with O(log n)/O(len) verify; pivots expected O(√n) or O(n); tournament expected O(n).

phases.goal: Avoid fixed seeds, weak hashes, XOR-on-multisets, and Monte Carlo/Las Vegas mix-ups.

must_hit.point: Never fixed seeds on CF open-hacking; avoid raw rand() / RAND_MAX — seed mt19937_64 from the clock so open hacks fail.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects fixed seeds and raw rand(); insists on clock-seeded mt19937_64.

must_hit.point: Using XOR as a multiset fingerprint — XOR only tracks parity/set membership; multisets need + mod a big prime (or 128-bit), as in Rearrange Query prefix sums.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags XOR-for-multiset and switches to sum-mod / 128-bit.

must_hit.point: Know Monte Carlo (tiny error OK, e.g. Zobrist) vs Las Vegas (always correct, runtime random) — do not treat a Zobrist equality as absolute certainty.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates Monte Carlo fingerprint error from Las Vegas always-correct random runtime.

must_hit.point: Default unordered_map without a custom/splitmix64 anti-hash can TLE under CF hacks; use a salted custom hash or map when TL allows.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names anti-hash / map as the fix for hackable unordered_map.

probes: What goes wrong if you XOR random ids to compare multisets?
How do Monte Carlo Zobrist checks differ from Las Vegas random pivots?

hints.1: Think about seed hacks, multiset vs set fingerprints, and whether error is allowed.
hints.2: Clock-seed; XOR≠multiset; Zobrist is Monte Carlo; salt unordered_map or use map.
hints.3: Say: never fixed seeds / raw rand(); multisets need + not XOR; Zobrist is Monte Carlo (tiny error OK) vs Las Vegas always-correct; splitmix64+salt or map against unordered_map hacks.

tradeoffs.topic: sort+compare vs Zobrist/sum-hash for multiset equality
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sort+compare is the safe interview answer for “same multiset on two windows.” Zobrist/sum-hash (ABC367F / Prefix Equality) is the CF speed trick: random ids with XOR for sets or prefix sums for multisets, equal fingerprints ⇒ equal structures w.h.p.

Monte Carlo allows tiny error (e.g. Zobrist fingerprint collisions) with usually fixed-ish runtime. Las Vegas is always correct with random runtime (random pivots / samples then verify), as in Interactive LowerBound or Quickselect intuition.
On CF, protect unordered_map/gp_hash_table with a custom hash (splitmix64 xor’d with a random salt) against open hacks/TLE. If TL allows, map is the simpler correct choice.

tradeoffs.topic: XOR set hash vs modular-sum multiset hash
tradeoffs.strong_answer: XOR of random 64-bit ids fingerprints sets / parity-multisets and toggles add/remove. Multisets need + mod a big prime (or 128-bit) instead of XOR so counts above 1 matter (Rearrange Query).

gotchas.trap: Fixed RNG seeds or raw rand()/RAND_MAX on CF.
gotchas.correction: Use mt19937_64 seeded from chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count() with uniform_int_distribution so open hacks fail.

gotchas.trap: Using XOR of random ids to compare general multisets.
gotchas.correction: XOR is for sets / parity; for multisets use + mod a big prime (or 128-bit), e.g. prefix sums in Rearrange Query.

gotchas.trap: Treating equal Zobrist fingerprints as absolute proof.
gotchas.correction: Zobrist is Monte Carlo: equal fingerprints ⇒ equal sets w.h.p., not certainty; prefer 64-bit or two independent hashes to keep birthday risk ~m²/M tiny.

gotchas.trap: Default unordered_map without an anti-hash on CF.
gotchas.correction: Custom hash (splitmix64 xor’d with a random salt) or use map when TL allows — otherwise TLE hacks (1005C-style).

gotchas.trap: Interactive solution without flush or ignoring judge -1.
gotchas.correction: Flush with endl / cout.flush(), respect query caps, and treat -1 as immediate exit.
